title: SOUTHERN TANZANIA BIRDING TOUR
summary: The Southern Tanzania Birding Tour can be combined with our Pemba Island endemic species. We also run camping trips in the remote Udzungwa Mountains, to search for forest specials; such as the endemic udzungwa forest patregide

itinerary.title: ARRIVAL IN TANZANIA
itinerary.description: Our Southern Tanzania Birding Tour will start in Tanzania’s economic capital, Dar es Salaam. On this day, if we have an early arrival, we may explore local attractions around Dar es Salaam. Otherwise, we can relax and enjoy the nice Tanzania birds from our lodge. Night in Dar es Salaam.

itinerary.title: DAR ES SALAAM TO MOROGORO
itinerary.description: The amazing Southern Tanzania Birding Tour will officially start today. We shall leave early and head west to the town of Morogoro. We shall enjoy birding on the way and we hope to start adding several special species on this route. On arrival, we shall continue birding around Morogoro, as we add more species of this interesting region. Night in Morogoro.

itinerary.title: UKAGURU MOUNTAINS
itinerary.description: On this day, we shall make a trip to a nearby but remote part of Tanzania- the Ukagurus, which is less visited by many birding tours. This area often produces surprises; and we can expect to find some exciting species to add to our Southern Tanzania Birding Tour. We shall spend the day here as we try our luck on these exciting species. Night in Ukaguru.

itinerary.title: AND 5: ULUGURU MOUNTAINS
itinerary.description: We shall move to the nearby Uluguru Mountains, where we shall be targeting the local endemics (Uluguru Greenbul, Winifred’s/ Mrs. Moreau’s Warbler, Loveridge’s Sunbird and Uluguru Bush-shrike); among an array of many other species. This area is remote and we hope to enjoy lots of rare birds, a key feature of our Southern Tanzania Birding Tour. We shall spend one night in the Ulugurus; then return to Morogoro on the second evening.

itinerary.title: TO IRINGA; VIA MIKUMI
itinerary.description: Our Southern Tanzania Birding Tour will continue West. We shall drive through Mikumi National Park as we head to Iringa. This will be a great opportunity to bird in the Miombo Woodland habitat around Mikumi; but we shall return to this area later on our tour. We shall make several stops as we scan for species along this very productive road. In the afternoon we shall continue our birding adventure around Iringa. Night in Iringa.

itinerary.title: UDZUNGWA SCARP AND ULUTI FOREST
itinerary.description: On this day we shall have an early start to scan another remote forest. We shall make a trip to Uluti Forest and the West Udzungwa Scarp; where we shall hope to spot the endemic Rufous-winged Sunbird. Many other rare birds occupy this forest and the nearby farms. This forest is often a major highlight on our Southern Tanzania Birding Tour. Night in Uluti.

itinerary.title: AND 9: RUAHA NATIONAL PARK
itinerary.description: We shall continue the Southern Tanzania Birding Tour to the vast Ruaha National Park. Ruaha is the largest national park in Tanzania, and it always amazes on each visit. We shall hope for some great mammal encounters as we enjoy the vast landscapes of this beautiful park. Local mammals, include Sable Antelope, Roan Antelope, African Lion, Leopard, Cheetah, Maasai Giraffe, Common Zebra, Common Eland, Common Impala and Bat-eared Fox. If we are really lucky we may spot the rare African Wild Dogs. Our eyes will be keen to look for bird’s species that we do not find on other locations during our Southern Tanzania Birding Tour. Nights at Ruaha.

itinerary.title: AND 11: UDZUNGWA MOUNTAINS NATIONAL PARK
itinerary.description: After a final birding session in Ruaha National Park, we shall drive onwards to Sanje; at the East Udzungwa Mountains. We shall enjoy birding here as we track extra forest species. On some sessions we may choose to make short drives to certain sections of this vast area that provide higher chances of seeing certain rarities. Nights at Udzungwa.

itinerary.title: KILOMBERO SWAMP TO MIKUMI NATIONAL PARK
itinerary.description: We shall enjoy a morning visit to a great location- where three Tanzanian endemics occur. Kilombero Swamp is always a highlight on our Southern Tanzania Birding Tour. We shall leave early and make a short trip to this very interesting floodplain where some birds’ species are yet to be fully described to science. These are Kilombero Cisticola, White-tailed Cisticola and Kilombero Weaver. Later we shall drive to the nearby Mikumi National Park, as we enjoy open country birds. Night in Mikumi.

itinerary.title: MIKUMI NATIONAL PARK
itinerary.description: The Miombo Woodland here is a fascinating habitat and allows birds’ species which will often be absent elsewhere in East Africa. This area will also allow us to add more big game to our already exciting Southern Tanzania Birding Tour species list. Mammals here include African Lion, Leopard, Ratel, Bushy-tailed Mongoose, Black-backed Jackal, African Wild Dog, Spotted Hyena, African Civet, African Elephant, Nile Hippopotamus, Maasai Giraffe, Bohor Reedbuck, Cape Buffalo and Blue Wildebeest. Night in Mikumi.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Arusha
itinerary.description: Arrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport and transfer to your lodge in Arusha. Spend the day relaxing and birdwatching around the lodge grounds, where you may spot species such as African Black Duck and Silvery-cheeked Hornbill.

itinerary.title: Arusha National Park
itinerary.description: Depart for Arusha National Park early in the morning. Explore the park’s diverse habitats, including montane forests and savannahs. Look for birds like the Bar-tailed Trogon, Grey-crowned Crane, and various sunbirds. Enjoy a picnic lunch amidst nature.

itinerary.title: Tarangire National Park
itinerary.description: Travel to Tarangire National Park, known for its large elephant herds and baobab trees. Birdwatching highlights include the Ashy Starling, Yellow-collared Lovebird, and various raptors. Spend the night at a lodge within or near the park.

itinerary.title: Tarangire National Park
itinerary.description: Continue exploring Tarangire with a full day of birding. Focus on different areas of the park to maximize your sightings. Look for species such as the Rufous-tailed Weaver and various migratory birds depending on the season.

itinerary.title: Lake Manyara National Park
itinerary.description: Head to Lake Manyara National Park, famous for its diverse ecosystems ranging from wetlands to woodlands. Birdwatchers can expect to see flamingos, pelicans, and many other waterfowl along with forest species like the Great Blue Turaco.

itinerary.title: Ngorongoro Crater
itinerary.description: Travel to Ngorongoro Crater, a UNESCO World Heritage site. While primarily known for its wildlife, birdwatchers can find unique species here such as the Kori Bustard and various raptors soaring above. Overnight at a lodge overlooking the crater.

itinerary.title: Ngorongoro Highlands
itinerary.description: Spend another day in the Ngorongoro region focusing on highland birds. Explore areas around Empakaai Crater or Olmoti Crater where you can find endemic species like the Usambara Eagle-Owl and other montane birds.

itinerary.title: Selous Game Reserve (Nyerere National Park)
itinerary.description: Depart for Selous Game Reserve (now Nyerere National Park), one of Africa’s largest protected areas. The reserve is home to numerous bird species including African Fish Eagles and various kingfishers along riversides.

itinerary.title: Selous Game Reserve (Nyerere National Park)
itinerary.description: Enjoy a full day of birding in Selous with options for boat safaris on the Rufiji River where you can observe aquatic birds as well as mammals. Look out for rare sightings such as Pel’s Fishing Owl.

itinerary.title: Departure from Dar es Salaam
itinerary.description: After breakfast, travel to Dar es Salaam for your departure flight or extend your trip with an optional visit to Pemba Island or Zanzibar if time allows.

summary: Western forest and lake-region birding across Mahale, Gombe, Burigi-Chato and Minziro.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Mahale National Park
itinerary.description: Arrive at the nearest airstrip or port and transfer to your accommodation. Spend the afternoon relaxing and acclimatizing to the environment. In the evening, enjoy a guided night walk to observe nocturnal bird species.

itinerary.title: Birding in Mahale National Park
itinerary.description: Early morning birdwatching session in the park’s diverse habitats. Look for species such as the African Fish Eagle (Haliaeetus vocifer) and various sunbirds. After lunch, take a boat trip on Lake Tanganyika to spot waterbirds like herons and kingfishers. Evening at leisure with an optional discussion on bird identification techniques.

itinerary.title: Gombe Stream National Park
itinerary.description: Depart early for Gombe Stream National Park, known for its rich biodiversity. Engage in birdwatching along the trails; target species include the Blue Monjita (Cyanomitra cyanolaema) and Olive Sunbird (Cyanomitra olivacea). Enjoy a picnic lunch amidst nature before continuing your exploration. Return to your accommodation for dinner and share your sightings of the day.

itinerary.title: Birding in Gombe Stream National Park
itinerary.description: Full day of birdwatching in Gombe. Focus on different trails to maximize species diversity. Look out for primate interactions while observing birds; this park is famous for its chimpanzees as well. Evening debrief with fellow birders to discuss findings and experiences.

itinerary.title: Travel to Burigi-Chato National Park
itinerary.description: Depart from Gombe early morning and travel towards Burigi-Chato National Park. Upon arrival, settle into your accommodation and prepare for an afternoon of exploration. Take a short evening walk around the park’s entrance area to spot local birds.

itinerary.title: Birding in Burigi-Chato National Park
itinerary.description: Spend a full day exploring Burigi-Chato’s diverse habitats including wetlands and forests. Target species include the Shoebill (Balaeniceps rex), Red-faced Barbet (Lybius rubrifacies), and migratory birds like Great Snipe (Gallinago media). Participate in guided walks focusing on specific areas known for high bird activity.

itinerary.title: Travel to Minziro Forest Reserve
itinerary.description: Depart from Burigi-Chato early morning heading towards Minziro Forest Reserve. After settling into accommodations, embark on an introductory birdwatching session within the reserve’s unique ecosystem.

itinerary.title: Birding in Minziro Forest Reserve
itinerary.description: Full day dedicated to exploring Minziro Forest. Focus on identifying endemic species found only within Kagera region such as various forest specials not seen elsewhere in Tanzania. Engage with local guides who can provide insights into both flora and fauna of this unique habitat. Evening discussions about conservation efforts related to logging impacts on local avifauna.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.description: Depending on flight schedules, enjoy one last morning of birdwatching or relax before departing from Minziro Forest back home or onward travel destinations.

title: 8 Days Birding Around Iringa
summary: Regional birding around Iringa including Kiponzero, Kisolanza, Uluti and Mufindi as listed on this route.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Iringa
itinerary.description: Arrive at Iringa and check into your accommodation. Spend the afternoon birding around the local area to acclimatize and spot common species such as the African Paradise Flycatcher and various weavers.

itinerary.title: Kiponzero Swamp
itinerary.description: Early morning departure to Kiponzero Swamp. Birding activities focusing on wetland species. Look for birds like the locust finch, fuellborn’s longclaw, rosy-throated longclaw, African snipe, gray-rumped swallow, Lesser Jacana, African Marsh Harrier, and various Cisticolas. Afternoon return to Iringa for a relaxing evening.

itinerary.title: Uluti Forest
itinerary.description: Depart early for Uluti Forest. Explore the forest trails while searching for forest specials such as the Livingstone’s Turaco, Iringa akalat, white-chested alethe, dapple-throat, swynnerton’s robin, white-winged apalis, rufous-winged sunbird and other endemic species. Enjoy a picnic lunch in the forest before continuing birding until late afternoon. Return to Iringa for dinner.

itinerary.title: Kisolanza Farm
itinerary.description: Morning drive to Kisolanza Farm. Birding around the farm area where you can find species like the Yellow-browed Seedeater and Uhehe Fiscal. Spend time observing both birds and local agricultural practices. Overnight stay at Kisolanza Farm.

itinerary.title: Mufindi Forest
itinerary.description: Depart for Mufindi Forest after breakfast. Engage in slow-paced birding throughout the day. Target species include Miombo Warbler, and various sunbirds. Take breaks to enjoy the scenic views of the highlands and possibly spot some mammals like Syke’s Monkey or bushbucks.

itinerary.title: Mufindi Highlands Exploration
itinerary.description: Full day of birding in Mufindi Highlands. Focus on highland specialties such as Iringa Akalat and Livingstone Flycatcher. Explore different habitats within the highlands including grasslands and wooded areas.

itinerary.title: Return to Iringa
itinerary.description: Morning birding session in Mufindi before heading back to Iringa. Stop at any promising locations along the way for additional birdwatching opportunities.

itinerary.title: Departure from Iringa
itinerary.description: Depending on your flight schedule, enjoy a final morning of birdwatching around Iringa or visit local markets before departing.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Arusha
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport, you will be greeted by a representative who will assist you with your transfer to Arusha Town. You will stay overnight at Eliboru Lodge, where you will receive a briefing about the upcoming birdwatching tour.

itinerary.title: Arusha National Park
itinerary.description: The day begins with pre-breakfast birdwatching around the lodge grounds, where you may spot various species such as fire finches and variable sunbirds. After breakfast, you’ll head to Arusha National Park for a full day of birding. The park is home to diverse bird species including Macoa ducks, Egyptian Geese, and Trogons. A walking safari will also provide opportunities to see White Fronted Bee-eaters and the rare Spike-heeled Lark.

itinerary.title: Journey to Serengeti
itinerary.description: After an early breakfast, you will embark on a long drive to the Serengeti National Park. During the journey, keep an eye out for Sand grouses and guinea fowls. Upon arrival in the evening, check into Ikoma Bush Tented Camp for dinner and overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Birdwatching in Serengeti
itinerary.description: Start your day with a pre-breakfast bird walk focusing on Tanzanian endemics like Fischer’s Lovebird and Grey-breasted Spurfowl. After breakfast, continue exploring the Serengeti for more bird species such as Usambiro Barbets and Grey-capped Social Weavers throughout the day.

itinerary.title: Ngorongoro Crater
itinerary.description: Depart from the Serengeti after breakfast and drive into Ngorongoro Crater. Here, look for endemic birds like Rufous-tailed Weaver and Golden-winged Sunbird while also enjoying sightings of large mammals such as elephants and various raptors soaring above.

itinerary.title: Lake Manyara National Park
itinerary.description: After breakfast, travel to Lake Manyara National Park known for its tree-climbing lions and diverse wildlife. Enjoy a picnic lunch within the park before continuing your exploration of its jungles where you can add more species to your list.

itinerary.title: Optional Activities at E Unoto Retreat
itinerary.description: You have the option for an early morning bird walk or spend the day game viewing in Lake Manyara or relaxing at your lodge with excellent birding opportunities from your balcony.

itinerary.title: Tarangire National Park
itinerary.description: Following breakfast, drive to Tarangire National Park with packed lunches. Focus on spotting Tanzanian endemics including Rufous-tailed Weaver and Yellow-collared Lovebird throughout your explorations in this park known for its high concentration of elephants.

itinerary.title: Full Day in Tarangire
itinerary.description: Spend an entire day exploring Tarangire Plains where you can observe numerous birds along with elephants. Return to your lodge for dinner after a fulfilling day of wildlife viewing.

itinerary.title: Departure from Arusha
itinerary.description: Depending on flight arrangements, there may be time for additional birdwatching in Tarangire before returning to Arusha for outbound connections.

itinerary.title: TARANGIRE NATIONAL PARK
itinerary.description: Following an early morning breakfast at your accommodation, you leave Arusha for Tarangire National Park. This park covering approximately 2600 square kilometers is spectacular in the dry season when many of the migratory wildlife species come back to the permanent waters of the Tarangire River. Huge herds of wildebeest, zebras, elephants, eland, and oryx gather to stay in Tarangire until the onset of the rains when they migrate again to good grazing areas. Expect to encounter large herds of elephants while here that are accustomed to vehicles. You will enjoy your lunch at the park and later have an evening game drive before heading to your accommodation for dinner and an overnight stay. Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner

itinerary.title: LAKE MANYARA NATIONAL PARK
itinerary.description: Following an early morning breakfast, you will depart for Lake Manyara National Park. Lake Manyara provides a perfect introduction to Tanzania’s birdlife. More than 400 species have been recorded, and even a first-time visitor to Africa might reasonably expect to observe 100 of these in one day. Inland of the floodplain, a narrow belt of acacia woodland is the favored haunt of Manyara’s legendary tree-climbing lions and impressively tusked elephants. Overnight will be at Lake Manyara Serena Lodge, a towering terracotta escarpment with panoramic views over the glittering alkaline waters of Lake Manyara. Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner

itinerary.title: SERENGETI NATIONAL PARK (NDUTU AREA)
itinerary.description: After breakfast, you will set off for the Ndutu area situated in the Ngorongoro conservation area, which is part of the southern Serengeti ecosystem. Lake Ndutu like most other rift lakes is alkaline however the water is still drinkable and consumed by a wide array of local wildlife. We will spend the afternoon with a game drive in the Ndutu area. The majority of the wildebeest migration can normally be found on the short-grass plains from December to April. The area is usually heavily populated with elephants, birds, and resident games. You will have dinner at your accommodation and an overnight stay. Meals: Breakfast, lunch, and dinner

itinerary.title: SERENGETI NATIONAL PARK (NDUTU AREA – SERONERA)
itinerary.description: Following an early morning breakfast, you will enjoy a full-day game drive in the Ndutu area exploring a great range of various habitats such as swamps, woodland, soda lakes, and the world-famous Serengeti short grass plains. You will witness herds of wildebeest and zebras, especially during a short time frame from around February and lasting for about 3 weeks where the majority of the wildebeest calve. While here, you will enjoy wildlife sightings with big games. The sea of grass provides little cover and the young make easy prey for a variety of predators. Wildebeest calves can run minutes after they were born and within 3 days, they are normally strong enough to keep up with the herd. Later in the afternoon, you will enjoy your trip back to Serengeti national park. Meals: Breakfast, lunch, and dinner

itinerary.title: SERENGETI NATIONAL PARK (SERONERA)
itinerary.description: After breakfast at your accommodation, you will proceed to the Central part of Serengeti. This park is well-known for its healthy stock of resident wildlife, particularly the “big five”, named for the five most prized trophies taken by hunters: Lion, Leopard, Elephant, Buffaloes, and Rhinos. You will enjoy wildlife sightings on your game drives in this wildlife-rich area before heading back for dinner and an overnight stay at your already booked accommodation. Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner

itinerary.title: NGORONGORO CRATER
itinerary.description: The other top area on this safari is the crater area. You start with an early morning game drive inside the Ngorongoro Crater. The Ngorongoro Conservation Area (NCA) is an extensive highland area along the eastern arm of the Rift Valley, with the world-renowned Ngorongoro Crater as its focal point. Ngorongoro was established to conserve wildlife and other natural resources. It also safeguards the interests of indigenous people and promotes tourism. While here, you will enjoy wildlife sightings with all the big games available. Meal Plan: Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner

itinerary.title: MTO WA MBU – ARUSHA
itinerary.description: After breakfast, we will drive Mto Wa Mbu for a morning cultural tour and a walking safari. We will have a sumptuous local lunch as we take in the stunning views hovering over us. An optional mountain biking activity can be arranged at an added cost if interested. In the late afternoon, you will head back to Arusha or to the airport for your flight back home. Meals: Breakfast & Lunch End of the 8 Days the Great Wildebeest Calving Migration Safari

The crater supports a year-round resident population of a variety of wildlife and you can easily spot lions, elephants, rhinos, buffalo, and other species of plain animals. itinerary.title: Day 4: SERENGETI NATIONAL PARK
itinerary.description: The following three days of your safari will be spent in Serengeti National Park, one of the top wildlife spots in the world. Our safari will take us via Olduvai Gorge. This is the prehistoric site where Dr. Louis Leakey discovered the remains of homo habilis, which is regarded as mankind’s first path of human evolution. An afternoon game drive at Serengeti follows home to more than 35 species of plains animals such as zebra, wildebeest, eland, giraffe, among many others. The park is the staging zone for one of the most spectacular events in the world- the annual migration of wildebeest. This commences around June when over 1 million wildebeest, zebra, and gazelle head for the Masai Mara in Kenya in search of greener pasture. They are followed closely by the predators of the savanna- lion, cheetah, wild dog, jackal, hyena, and vultures. The Serengeti also has over 500 species of birds. itinerary.title: Arusha
itinerary.description: After arrival at Kilimanjaro Airport, we head to a lodge near Arusha National Park.

itinerary.title: Arusha NP
itinerary.description: We’ll spend the day on Mt. Meru, which looms over Arusha. The mix of habitats here includes montane forest, and offers us many exciting birds including Crowned Hawk-Eagle, Cinnamon-chested Bee-eater, and splendid songster Rueppell’s Robin-Chat. As we head up the mist-shrouded slopes, the yellowwood trees become draped in Usnea old man’s beard lichen and we search for skulking gems such as White-starred Robin and the dapper Brown Woodland-Warbler. The park is also an excellent place to find large herds of buffalo grazing the mountain’s lower slopes, not to mention a remarkable abundance of giraffes and a chance for scarce forest antelope like Harvey’s duiker.

itinerary.title: Arusha District
itinerary.description: We drive around the looming Mt. Meru to the lark plains. These grasslands are home to the last 100 or so Beesley’s Larks on Earth, and we will search long and hard for this critically endangered Tanzanian endemic. Other interesting species here include Chestnut-bellied and Yellow-throated Sandgrouse, shrikes, migrant wheatears, pipits, and larks galore. The plains are lined by Drepanolobium whistling thorn trees, while hills offer a scrubby habitat that can deliver Red-fronted and Black-throated Barbets, Red-throated Tit, Eremomelas, and Crombecs. Thicket habitat and riparian strips offer many great birds, including Slate-colored Boubou, Nubian Woodpecker, the highly gregarious Gray-headed Social-Weaver, and the possibility of migrants like Spotted Flycatcher and Common Nightingale.

itinerary.title: Day 4: Tarangire National Park
itinerary.description: From Arusha we head to Tarangire, where we shall enjoy some of northern Tanzania’s finest birding. The low baobab-clad plains and fever-tree groves here support many cool species including three Tanzanian endemics and near-endemics: Ashy Starling, Yellow-collared Lovebird, and Rufous-tailed Weaver. The lush grasses are full of ground birds like Northern White-bellied Bustard and both Red-necked and Yellow-necked Francolins. This is one of the better places to see elephants, which can occur in great numbers along the Tarangire River. We also stand a good chance of seeing our first lions, and maybe even a leopard or cheetah.

itinerary.title: Tarangire to Ngorongoro Crater
itinerary.description: After leaving Tarangire, we’ll stay in the Rift Valley, spending most of the day birding the fabulous Lake Manyara National Park. This diverse gem of a park holds lush forest with Silvery-cheeked Hornbill and Crowned Eagle, vast mudflats which might be covered in migrating shorebirds, and marshes that support the likes of African Swamphen and a range of herons and egrets. This park is also good for mammals like African Buffalo and Hippo. Around mid-afternoon, we’ll drive up the western Rift escarpment, wind through some pleasant agricultural areas, then enter the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Our lodge here enjoys spectacular panoramic views of what might be the world’s most famous wildlife preserve, and with good reason.

itinerary.title: Ngorongoro Crater
itinerary.description: We have a full day to explore the magical Ngorongoro, though in the morning we won’t be in a hurry to descend into the crater, as the forest and heath along the rim offers excellent birding. We’ll keep our eyes peeled for flowering Leonotis, if we find a patch, we might be get to savor the coolest sunbird spectacle in Africa: the impressive Golden-winged, coppery-colored Bronze, and iridescent-purple Tacazee Sunbirds all competing for nectar from the same flowers. Descending into the crater with its towering vertical walls is like finding Africa’s Garden of Eden. Inside, we seek myriad grassland and woodland birds, as well as scavenging vultures amidst a thronging wildlife spectacle virtually unequalled on earth. Thirty thousand-some big mammals are resident here, and a decent proportion of them can be seen from a single view point within the crater, an indescribably magnificent sight.

itinerary.title: Day 9: Ndutu
itinerary.description: From the crater rim,we move through the Malanja depression and onto the Serengeti plains, where sandgrouse, bustards, and larks abound. Grant’s gazelles are scattered across the plains, while Ostrich and giraffe walk swaying in the haze. Towards Ndutu we enter beautiful mature Acacia woodland with alkaline lakes and swamps. The lodge’s waterhole is a bird magnet with ever-present Fischer’s Lovebird, a variety of bishops, waxbills, and widowbird, and the endemic Gray-breasted Francolin. The woodlands harbor Rufous Chatterer, Cardinal and Bearded Woodpeckers, Black-faced Babbler, and Green Wood hoopoe. With a bit of luck, and depending on the rains, the wildebeest will have recently calved in this area, and up to half a million females may be in attendance with their young, presenting a wildlife spectacle of awesome proportions, impossible to describe and enthralling to experience. itinerary.title: Arusha – Tarangire National Park
itinerary.description: In 5 days, Tanzania camping safari, after a safari briefing in the morning, you will travel southwest towards the Tarangire National Park. With its interesting landscapes – from swamps to baobab trees – it is considered as one of the most beautiful parks in northern Tanzania. Elephants can be seen in herds of up to 600, along with wildebeests, Masai giraffes, buffaloes and zebras. You will enjoy an extensive game drive until you leave the park in the late afternoon to travel to the Lake Burunge Tented Camp, where you will overnight. Lunch; Dinner

itinerary.title: Tarangire Area
itinerary.description: Lake Manyara National Park – Karatu After breakfast you will travel from the Tarangire Area to the Lake Manyara National Park. The park is known for its over 400 bird species, primate-filled forests and grassy plains. A large area of the park is covered by the alkaline Lake Manyara, the seasonal breeding grounds for large colonies of flamingos and many more waterfowls. The park is also home to giraffes, hippos, wildebeests, impalas and groups of noisy monkeys and baboons. After an extensive game drive, you will travel to Karatu in the Ngorongoro highlands. After your arrival, there might be time for an optional walk in the coffee plantations to learn more about coffee production. You will spend the night at one of the three beautifully located Tanganyika Wilderness Adventure Lodges.Breakfast; Lunch; Dinner

itinerary.title: Karatu
itinerary.description: Ngorongoro Crater – Serengeti National Park Rise and shine! After breakfast you will drive to the crater rim from where you will take on the steep and adventurous trail into the crater. Here, within a few square kilometres, you can find all the animals that live in the East African savannah. You will see a diversity of wildlife ranging from the “Big Five” – lion, elephant, buffalo, rhino and leopard – to wildebeests, Grant’s and Thomson’s gazelles and mountain reedbucks in the forests on the slopes. The crater is also one of the best places to see the magnificent but almost extinct black rhino. You will spend the morning on a game drive followed by a picnic lunch. During the early afternoon, you will leave the crater and travel to the Serengeti. The Serengeti National Park is the most famous park in Tanzania and it is here where the biggest animal migration in the world takes place. Herds of wildebeests and zebras cross the border between Tanzania and Kenya in search of fresh grass and water and predators are never far behind. Tonight, you will stay at the Kati Kati Tented Camp in the central Serengeti. Breakfast; Lunch; Dinner

itinerary.title: Serengeti National Park
itinerary.description: After sunrise you will leave the camp for an early morning game drive and return in the late morning to a hearty breakfast. Alternatively, adventurous guests can experience the Serengeti from the sky when joining a hot air balloon ride, followed by a champagne breakfast. This activity is optional and needs to be booked in advance. Those interested in seeing the visitor central are also able to do so. Depending on time there will be another game drive in the afternoon before you return to the Kati Kati Tented Camp to spend another night. Breakfast; Lunch; Dinner

itinerary.title: Serengeti National Park – Lake Victoria
itinerary.description: After an early start, you will continue through the Serengeti National Park on your way out. There will be more time to spot animals you may not have seen already, perhaps the rare African wild dog? The Serengeti is also home to the “Big Five” – lion, elephant, buffalo, rhino and leopard – and today you might be able to tick off all the members of this group. After leaving the park, the journey continues to Lake Victoria, the largest lake in Africa and the second largest in the world. The area around Lake Victoria is the most fertile and densely inhabited region of Tanzania. Here at the ocean-like lake, you will see another side of Tanzania – away from the masses you will experience how the local people live. You can take a walk along the lake shore and watch fishermen at work – an experience unavailable on the usual tourist routes. You will overnight at the Speke Bay Lodge. Breakfast; Lunch; Dinner

itinerary.title: Lake Victoria – Masai Mara Area
itinerary.description: After breakfast you will join the local fishermen and a guide on a canoe trip on Lake Victoria. You will see how the locals catch fish the traditional way and admire the previous night’s catch. Back on dry land you will depart on the longest journey of your safari – the trip to the Masai Mara. The road towards the Kenyan border is a long and adventurous one, but it should be worth it as the “Mara” is reputed to have the highest lion population of all reserves in Africa. Other large cats also live here and can be spotted all year round, as their sightings are not dependent upon the seasons or the great migration. You will overnight in safari tents at Mara West Camp on the outskirts of the reserve. Breakfast; Lunch; Dinner

itinerary.title: + 8 Masai Mara Game Reserve
itinerary.description: The next two days are dedicated to game viewing in the Masai Mara Game Reserve. You will also take a trip to the Mara River, the greatest hurdle for the wildebeests and zebras on their yearly trek. An incredible scene is set when the river has swollen to almost bursting levels. Thousands of animals must cross it, risking death as crocodiles wait below the surface of the swirling water. It can be a gruesome sight. At other times of the year, hippos, hungry crocodiles and other animals can also be seen at the river. You will spend two nights at the Ashnil Mara Camp. Breakfast; Lunch; Dinner

itinerary.title: Masai Mara Game Reserve – Lake Nakuru National Park
itinerary.description: After breakfast you will leave the Mara to reach Lake Nakuru National Park in the early afternoon. The shallow alkaline lake attracts seasonally flocks of flamingos. Not only can you see over 450 bird species and 50 mammals, but you might spot both the endangered white and black rhino. Other animals in the park include waterbucks, buffaloes, Rothschild’s giraffes, lions, cheetahs and leopards as well as troops of baboons and monkeys and lots of pythons hanging around in the trees. Tonight, you will stay at the Flamingo Hill Camp.Breakfast; Lunch; Dinner

itinerary.title: Lake Nakuru National Park – Nairobi
itinerary.description: After breakfast you will leave the Lake Nakuru National Park to travel southeast towards Nairobi, Kenya’s bustling and often chaotic capital. You will arrive in the early afternoon and depending on the rest of your travel plans, you will be taken to the city center or directly to the airport. Breakfast; Lunch
